core.text: One observed 300 rpm trial achieved approximately 2.4 percent final-vial spread after stopping at second 60. This challenges universal necessity of sustained 900 rpm, but repeatability and the cause of image fluctuations remain hypotheses.

Propose three alternative arms, twice each within six trials: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds; fixed 600 rpm for 60 seconds; and four 20 mL low-to-high syringe transfers completed at seconds 15, 30, 45 and 60 without rotation. Run 300, 600, syringe, syringe, 600, 300. Lower speed, intermediate speed and directed bulk transport are candidate approaches; none has established repeatable success.

Use the stipulated recipe, fresh rinsed vessel, fixed addition location, same dye bottle, locked camera and spill tray. End mixing at second 60, then sample at second 120 with the specified depths and withdrawal window. Alternate depth order between each arm’s two repeats. Stop on escaping liquid.

Log five-second image spread without allowing it to change operation. Report raw vial attenuations, normalized spread, target failures, stirring seconds, transfer counts and cessation times. Hypothesize that at least one alternative meets the at-most-4-percent sample proxy in both repeats. Compare agitation demand only among tested arms; report syringe effort separately rather than treating zero stirring as zero work.

residue.text: Speck counts and depression can describe optical disturbance but cannot identify bubbles. Any association between disturbance and vial success remains exploratory.

Directed transfers might improve vertical transport, but can also disturb gradients and complicate sampling interpretation. Common-aliquot references assess repeatability, not concentration calibration; two repeats cannot settle causal attribution.

Matched 900 rpm final samples and its total duration are absent, preventing comparative uniformity or time-saving claims against the preferred procedure. Commanded speed is unverified; extension beyond this recipe is untested.

tension.account_a: Hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds reliably suffices for the bounded final-sample proxy, despite earlier side-image spread.
tension.account_b: Incompatible rival hypothesis: fixed 300 rpm for 60 seconds does not reliably suffice; residual depth gradients require greater or differently directed redistribution.
tension.prediction_a: Both 300 rpm repeats should yield final-vial spread at most 4 percent despite varying side images and opposite sampling orders; intermediate speed or transfers need not improve target attainment.
tension.prediction_b: Repeated 300 rpm failures above 4 percent, alongside repeated success of 600 rpm or syringe transport, would favor inadequate redistribution. Order-dependent failures or failure of all arms would leave the accounts unresolved.
